chunks: If a man leaves behind a wife and grandchildren, then the wife receives one-eighth, and whatever remains belongs to the grandchildren.
If a woman leaves behind her husband and grandchildren, then the husband receives one-fourth, and whatever remains belongs to the grandchildren.

This is because the husband and wife are not two primary heirs; rather, they inherit by way of cause, not by way of lineage. So the grandchildren, along with them, take the place of the child, because the deceased has neither child nor parents.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْوَلَدِ: in the position or legal standing of a child
key_terms.مِنْ جِهَةِ السَّبَبِ: by reason of a legal cause, here marriage
key_terms.وَارِثَيْنِ أَصْلِيَّيْنِ: primary heirs by direct blood relation
key_terms.وَلَدَ الْوَلَدِ: grandchildren or descendants of one's children

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a spouse and grandchildren when there are no children or parents?
ai.summary: This legal ruling explains the inheritance shares when the deceased leaves a spouse and grandchildren but no direct children or parents. The spouse receives the fixed Qur'anic share, while the remainder goes to the grandchildren, who stand in the place of the deceased's children in this case.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
"If a man dies and leaves behind a wife and grandchildren (descendants of his children), the wife receives one-eighth of the inheritance, and the remainder goes to the grandchildren.
If a woman dies and leaves behind her husband and grandchildren, the husband receives one-fourth of the inheritance, and the remainder goes to the grandchildren.
This division is because the husband and wife are not considered primary heirs by blood; rather, they inherit through marital relation, not through lineage. Therefore, the grandchildren take the position of the direct children when there are no surviving children or parents of the deceased."
